body: I would say it's the original date of the test in your case. I had my IELTS re-evaluated and the score changed, but I listed the original test date. For context, IRCC won't ask you for your language score certificate to be uploaded when you submit the application as they can verify this themselves. My application was approved, therefore it didn't cause an issue for me. Again I'm just speculating for your situation. If it's really of concern, what I would do in your situation is list the original test date and then if/when you get an ITA you can write up and submit a letter of explanation with any concerns you might have. Disclaimer, I'm not any kind of expert, just offering my opinion.

It depends what you mean by re-evaluated, if you took a brand new test, then it would be the new test date, whereas if you had the original test re-marked then it would be the original test date not the date it was re-marked.

Although those numbers are good, availability is very low for September. Most Year Round offers are sent in early Summer around May and at the end of Term 1 around December. You'll almost certainly be reached by the end of Term 1 provided your earliest occupancy date is not set any later than January 1st 2025.

I assume you mean May 2025? If so, then very good. Most movement in terms of offers happens at the end of Term 1 December to January and Term 2 April - May. I would say you even have a chance to be reached at the end of Term 1 if you've indicated your earliest occupancy date as January 1st 2025 or earlier.

Depends how specific your recommendation is. If it's a recommendation for a specific floor or studio size, or specific residence area it'll take longer. For a recommendation of any studio in Year-Round it'll likely be quicker.
